author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: The allocation logic for the committed pallets must pass a formal sign off on the acceptance criteria before the trucks leave the distribution centre. This is not a preference. The supplier has already confirmed the bulk order, and the physical stock is locked in for the promotion week. If we ship without that strict governance layer, we have no auditable trail to prove the logic was sound when the money was committed. I will not allow the feature to go live until that formal review is complete and documented. The manual checks are not enough for this scale of financial exposure. We need the sign off to be fully governed to protect the company from liability if the allocation misses.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly refuses to allow the feature to go live without the formal sign-off, establishing a non-negotiable line that crossing would result in refusal.
